rules_inferred: cloud snapshot = nearest numeric EngineCoolantTemp row in +-120 s; 1169 rows total
clean = ens_outlier_v2 False (NaN not clean); obd coolant from th.obd_coolant on raw matched by digits; 710 drives have the channel
K1 age = snapshot time - time of last OBD sample (not t1)
K2 unit end = end of last accepted step; logged cloud km = accepted steps wholly inside [t0,t1]; terciles by np.digitize on percentiles 33.3/66.7 of logged km

K3 anchor time = last OBD sample (S_obd) or snapshot time; parked = first OBD sample of b - anchor; D anchor = last accepted step in [end a, start b]; Tamb = mean ambientByDrive[b]; primary 0-6 h, 0.25 h lower bound
Sen through origin = median(y/x); with intercept = median pairwise slopes, intercept = median(y - slope*x); bootstrap resamples arrival days, 4000, seed 42, numpy default_rng
concerns: K1 day-bootstrap interval of the median is degenerate [-2,-2] (integer data, 133 days): report mean with interval too; offset -2 C is stable, rule 'consistent' fails on median|d|<=2 only marginally (equals 2) but interval-within-+-1 fails
K1 slope -1.9 C/min of d on age is large and implies cloud reads lower with age or OBD last-sample clock anchoring error; age is confounded by the master-start-anchored OBD clock

Through-origin vs intercept k differ by about 0.1-0.14 per h (intercepts -0.1 to -0.19): k is fit-model dependent; D_cloud below 20-pair-ish support in days (28 days, 29 pairs, ok above floor but fragile)
Exact tie-breaking for equidistant snapshots, tercile boundary and D step selection are my choices; unspecified in spec
